0.long_answer: The causal gene of Allan–Herndon–Dudley syndrome that has been shown to be mutated in cases of X-linked leukoencephalopathy is the MCT8 gene, which is also known as SLC16A2. This gene encodes the monocarboxylate transporter 8, a protein essential for the cellular transport of thyroid hormones such as T3 and T4 across cell membranes. Mutations in MCT8 disrupt the proper distribution of thyroid hormones, leading to neurological abnormalities, and have been implicated in the pathology of both Allan–Herndon–Dudley syndrome and X-linked leukoencephalopathy.
